title: Midday scrim — sprint micro-decisions & launch checklist
content:
11:30 AM — midday capture (quick, noisy, honest)

Context: small-surface launch for hosted API change (prefix caching defaults + token billing clarifications). Need to land PRD edits, confirm infra runbook, and lock canary percentages before EOD.

Top outcomes I want today:
- PRD ready for engineering (ACs and optional rollback criteria explicit)
- Infra runbook checked with SRE + warm path smoke tests queued
- Canary rollout configured, baseline dashboards ready, alert thresholds set
- Stakeholders aligned (Legal sign-off on privacy blurb, Support briefed)

PRD edits to finish (open items) — current draft sections I touched this morning:
- Acceptance criteria: convert vague perf targets into measurable SLOs (latency p50/p95, token cost delta < 15%) — need numbers from infra team (Sofia).
- Migration note: describe optional prefix-cache toggle + migration data retention (add KMS note) — action: Marco to confirm KMS key id and access flow.
- Rollback conditions: add explicit triggers (error spike > 3x baseline, p95 latency > 2s for 5 min) — decide exact thresholds with Nate.
- API surface change docs: small paragraph for SDK teams about new header behavior; include code sample.

Open questions (putting them here before the 1:15 sync)
- Q: Does Dedicated tier need a separate rollout policy? (I think yes — slower ramp + notify customers). Will ask Ben in contract ops.
- Q: Are we comfortable with 10% initial canary for hosted in us-west? or do we start 5%? My read: 5% safer given KV cache state; ask SRE.
- Q: Do Support and Documentation have time to update KB + changelog before launch? If not, we need a temporary copy embedded in the console.

Quick meeting notes (09:20 sync with eng & infra)
- Sofia: can provide perf numbers by noon; will try to nail down p95 baseline with current quantization profile.
- Nate (SRE): wants explicit smoke test list and a quick script to run against canary nodes. Will own alert thresholds.
- Marco (Design): will produce a single-line summary for the UI and a compact SDK snippet by 4p.

Action items (my prioritized todo)
- [ ] Finalize PRD ACs (write exact SLO numbers) — owner: me (Aisha) — ETA: 15:00
- [ ] Confirm KMS key workflow with Marco — owner: Marco — ETA: 17:00 (he said maybe earlier)
- [ ] Add rollback thresholds to runbook (discuss w/ Nate) — owner: Nate + me — ETA: 16:00
- [ ] Create canary dashboard (base rates + error budget) — owner: Nate — ETA: EOD
- [ ] Draft support KB + console message (minimal) — owner: Support (cc: me) — ETA: before launch
- [ ] Add SDK note and small code example to API docs — owner: SDK docs — ETA: 4p

Launch checklist (short, to be copy-pasted into the runbook)
- Pre-launch: smoke tests green locally, perf metrics within expected variance, deploy knobs present
- Canary: 5% initial traffic -> monitor 30m -> 20% -> 60% -> full (only if all green and no regressions)
- Alerts: set p95 latency + error rate + token-cost-per-request spikes, page SRE on threshold breach
- Rollback: automated toggle (feature flag) + manual rollback playbook + PR rollback link in runbook
- Post-launch: 24h watch, then 72h check-in for regressions and cost delta review

Notes to self / follow-ups I won't forget:
- Ping Ben about Dedicated tier policy (contract implications).
- Remind Legal to answer the privacy blurb question — low risk but needs doc trace.
- Add a short blurb in PRD under 'communication' about how we message the change to devs (transparent about cache behavior).

Mental model checklist (why this matters)
- Small API surface changes have outsized customer friction if docs/support aren't synced.
- Cache changes can shift tail latency and cost — need early telemetry and cautious canaries.
- Team alignment (one clear owner per artifact) reduces late-night triage.

End-of-day micro-plan (what I'll do 4–6p)
- 4:00pm: merge PRD edits if Sofia/Nate confirm numbers
- 4:30pm: quick dry-run of smoke tests with Nate on staging canary nodes
- 5:15pm: draft the console copy + KB minimal patch (if docs lag)
- 5:45pm: final stakeholder ping (Legal, Support, Contract ops) and sign-off capture

Random scratch snippets (for later)
- Consider a tiny experiment: default caching on for dev accounts only for 2 weeks to gather telemetry without affecting prod.
- Keep a short 'what-we-learned' note after 48h — capture token-cost delta and p95 shift.

---
Saved here as a noisy personal capture; will clean and move key pieces into the official PRD and runbook once numbers come in.
